descZh: 1939 年夏，法国情报机构获得德军 Enigma 密码机的密钥资料与操作说明，经波兰转交英国。这批文件让布莱切利园得以系统研究德军加密体制，成为盟军破译 Enigma、赢得大西洋战役的关键起点。
descEn: In the summer of 1939, French intelligence obtained German Enigma key materials and operating manuals, which were passed on to Britain via Poland. These documents let Bletchley Park study the German cipher system systematically, making them the crucial starting point for breaking Enigma and winning the Battle of the Atlantic.
textZh: 1939 年 7 月，在波兰即将沦陷之际，波兰密码局将 Enigma 复原机与破译成果移交给英法。法国情报员古斯塔夫·贝特朗随后把截获的德军密钥资料与密码本交给英国，其中包含真实密钥表与操作流程。布莱切利园正是借助这些资料，结合图灵的 Bombe 设计，从 1940 年起持续破译德军密电，最终改变了二战进程。
textEn: In July 1939, as Poland was about to fall, the Polish Cipher Bureau handed reconstructed Enigma machines and their breakthroughs to Britain and France. French intelligence officer Gustave Bertrand then delivered captured German key documents, including genuine key tables and procedures, to Britain. Using these materials and Turing's Bombe design, Bletchley Park decrypted German traffic from 1940 onward, changing the course of World War II.

eraZh: 1940 年代 · 英国布莱切利园
descZh: 德军 Enigma 操作员为图省事，常选择容易的转子设置与密钥，如 AAA、ABC 或女友名字。布莱切利园破译员戏称这些偷懒密码为「cillies」，并以此作为推测当日密钥的捷径，大幅加快破译速度。
descEn: German Enigma operators, seeking convenience, often chose easy rotor settings and keys such as AAA, ABC, or girlfriends' names. Bletchley Park cryptanalysts jokingly called these lazy keys "cillies" and used them as shortcuts to deduce the day's key, greatly speeding up decryption.
textZh: 德军规定每日更换 Enigma 密钥，但操作员习惯偷懒：把三个转子设为 AAA、ABC 之类的连续字母，或使用可预测的初始位置。布莱切利园把这些可猜的密钥称为「cillies」（对 silly 的戏称）。破译员利用这种人性的弱点排除大量组合，甚至先猜密钥再验证，使 Bombe 的搜索空间骤减，成为密码史上「人是最薄弱环节」的经典案例。
textEn: German regulations demanded daily Enigma key changes, but operators habitually cheated: setting the three rotors to AAA, ABC, or other predictable positions. Bletchley Park called these guessable keys "cillies" (a pun on "silly"). By exploiting this human weakness, codebreakers eliminated huge numbers of combinations — sometimes guessing the key first and verifying it later — shrinking the Bombe's search space dramatically. It remains a classic case of the human factor being the weakest link in cryptography.

nameZh: 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文
eraZh: 1969 年 · 美国旧金山湾区
descZh: 1969 年 11 月，自称「黄道十二宫」的连环杀手向《旧金山纪事报》寄出密文，宣称其中 13 个字符暗藏他的真实姓名。五十年间无数人尝试破解，至今未获公认答案，成为悬案中最著名的未解密码之一。
descEn: In November 1969, the self-styled "Zodiac" serial killer mailed a cipher to the San Francisco Chronicle, claiming 13 of its characters concealed his real name. Fifty years of attempts have produced no generally accepted solution, making it one of the most famous unsolved ciphers in history.
textZh: 这封「我的名字是」信件中，13 个字符据称代表凶手的真名。业余与专业密码学家提出过数百种解法，从斯拉夫姓氏到精巧的拼图，但没有任何一种得到官方与公众的一致认可。即使 FBI 在 2020 年宣布破解 340 字符的 z340 密文时，也明确表示这 13 字符仍未解开，令其成为密码史上最令人着迷的悬案之一。
textEn: In the "My Name Is" letter, 13 characters allegedly spelled the killer's true identity. Amateur and professional cryptanalysts have proposed hundreds of solutions, from Slavic surnames to elaborate puzzles, but none has won official or public acceptance. Even when the FBI announced the 2020 solution of the 340-character z340 cipher, it stated that these 13 characters remain unbroken — keeping them among cryptography's most intriguing mysteries.

nameZh: Enigma M4 海军四转子密码机
descZh: 1942 年初，德国海军为 U 型潜艇装备四转子 Enigma M4，在标准三转子之外增设希腊字母转子，使密钥空间暴增。大西洋狼群战术因此一度畅行无阻，盟军直到年底才借助缴获的密钥资料攻破 M4，扭转护航战局。
descEn: In early 1942, the German Navy equipped U-boats with the four-rotor Enigma M4, adding a Greek-letter rotor to the standard three and vastly expanding the key space. The wolf-pack tactic flourished until the Allies finally broke the M4 late that year, turning the tide of convoy warfare.
textZh: 三转子 Enigma 被破译后，德国海军于 1942 年 2 月启用 M4：额外的一个转子让组合数增长 26 倍，并专门用于潜艇通信。U 型潜艇一度在北大西洋重创盟军船队，每月击沉数十万吨运输船。直到 1942 年 10 月，英军从 U-559 号潜艇上缴获 M4 密钥与短信号本，布莱切利园才重新掌握海神密码的钥匙，大西洋之战自此转折。
textEn: After the three-rotor Enigma was broken, the German Navy introduced the M4 in February 1942: one extra rotor multiplied the combinations by 26 and was reserved for submarine traffic. U-boats devastated Allied convoys in the North Atlantic, sinking hundreds of thousands of tons of shipping each month. Not until October 1942, when British sailors captured M4 key materials and the short-signal book from U-559, did Bletchley Park regain the key to the Triton cipher — and the Battle of the Atlantic turned.
